A Sub-Saharan African national and recent Ph.D. graduate in Economic History, I bring five years of experience building production-grade AI and data systems across Europe to a deeply personal commitment to development on the African continent. Born in southern Africa and raised across Eswatini, Zambia, and South Africa, I have seen first-hand how data — and the absence of it — shapes economic opportunity. From deploying NLP pipelines that help workers claim fair wages, to digitising African public finance records that were previously inaccessible to researchers, I have consistently used technology to expand access to information. I am eager to bring these skills to the World Bank's mission of reducing poverty and increasing shared prosperity, and to invest in the next generation of African researchers and policymakers.
